main_text.l: Vt si quis magno iubeat quandoque theatro
Fabros artifices ve alios consurgere, summum
Tollere vel digitum, nemo consurgat opinor
Præter eos tantum quos præco surgere iussit.
Iusserit idem omnes sapientes surgere, nemo
Sede sua maneat, nemo non erigat alte
In cælum caput, & numerari noluit in illis:
Atq; adeo vitio hoc hominum pars magna
laborat. Nulla quidem Scythicis tam barbara natio
terris, Quæ se non meliora sequi, non optima credat,
Cui sua non summe placeant, quæ denique
leges Permutare suas alienis legibus optet.
Nec res vsurpata hominum minus vlla querelis
Ad superos, precibúsve minus votísque petita,
Quàm dono concessa Deùm sapientiæ tantam
Vnusquisque sibi diuino e munere partem
Adrogat, & tanto sese dignatur honore.
Qui modò ludus erat pueris, & nota per vrbem
Fabula, quem rifit coniunx, risere ministri,
Ipse domi plaudit
sibi solus, sequeque tuetur,
Ac si præcipiti vicisset Olympia cursu:
Contentúsque suo tanquam meliore videtur
Iudicio linguam, atque alienas spernere voces:
Interea nullus toto est in corpore sensus,
Nulla mali vel suspicio, vel cura latentis.
Tantus amor, tanta est animis fiducia nostri!
Miretur reges nemo peccare, quibus tot
Peccandi authores, tot causas esse videmus.

page.notes: The first lines of several verses begin with a decorative ornament before the initial word ("Atq;", "Ad", "Adrogat", "Ac si"); I have transcribed the words without it. The printed "Ad superos" and "Ac si" are kept as printed. Stanza breaks are marked by my reading of the indented lines, so the paragraph divisions are approximate. The line "Quàm dono concessa Deùm sapientiæ tantam" is partly unclear at the join and is read as printed. The printed "vsurpata" and "Deùm" are kept as printed; the spelling of u/v has been normalised elsewhere.
